Conclusions
Medical nutrition therapy is essential to all people with diabetes, of whatever type or severity. A healthy diet should contain impor-
tant components, including foods containing carbohydrates from whole grains, fruits, vegetables, vitamins, and low-fat dairy prod-
ucts. Although blood glucose control and management of coexisting risk factors are overall goals, the implementation of dietary
management is a highly complex and individualized process. Principles of medical nutrition therapy that generally apply to all dia-
betes, and speciﬁc features that apply to the various types of diabetes, have been discussed; but it must be emphasized that good
nutritional management requires the close interaction of each individual patient with a knowledgeable expert in dietetics.
